narrative: Your application was denied because the model estimated a 66.5% chance you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. This high probability of failure drove the rejection. The most influential factor in this prediction was your LSAT score. Although it was the strongest factor overall, it actually worked in your favor: your score of 38 was slightly above the average of 37.18 for accepted students, pushing the prediction toward passing. However, the next two most important factors both pushed strongly toward failure. Your ranking in the bottom decile of your class in Year 3 (decile 2 versus an average of about 5.8 for accepted students) was the second most influential feature, and your Year 1 ranking (also decile 2 versus an average of 6) was third. These very low class rankings signal a high risk of bar exam failure. Your family income (middle bracket) and full-time work status were less influential. To improve your chances, focus on raising your academic performance in law school, particularly in upper-year courses, and consider retaking the LSAT if possible. You may also want to seek academic support and discuss your situation with an admissions advisor.
